core_actor_bases.name: Actor
core_actor_bases.role: implicit actor nominal; not an ordinary guest-constructible class

core_actor_bases.name: SupervisorActor
core_actor_bases.role: runtime-validated supervisor; CONTROL callbacks never ordinary callable methods

core_actor_bases.name: ServiceActor<Request,Reply>
core_actor_bases.role: typed request/reply actor, does not turn Service trait into mailbox authority

security_invariants: Actor base conformance never grants supervisor CONTROL, actor spawning, or mailbox sender identity
Only runtime-minted ActorRef and channel endpoints authorize delivery; plain IDs or structural methods do not
Actor lifecycle init and receive are private runtime-only external ingress, never public guest-callable methods
Actor-owned mutable state is sealed and accessed only by checked critical-read/critical-write; no raw state references escape or survive await
Each actor has serialized effective turns, immutable incarnation identity and generation-fenced mailbox admission
Panic uses trusted supervisor priority CONTROL and cannot be intercepted by the actor that panicked
Actor or trait implementers cannot provide their own Sendable, Drop, Receives or ActorLifecycle safety proof
ores.core imports no ores.std or OS facilities; hosted bases require explicit runtime permissions and nonblocking I/O
Async Read/Write/Source/Sink/KeyValueStore do not imply concrete I/O implementations or durable completion
Cancellation, close, start failure and supervisor crash settle pending futures and release bounded quotas exactly once
Serial HTTP means concurrency policy requestConcurrency=1,messageConcurrency=1, not a new privileged actor species
